raw:
{
  "question_intent": "Inquire about the new baseline for US card NIM and its future stability, and seek clarification on hedge income booking complexities.",
  "main_topics": ["US card NIM baseline", "NIM stability", "Hedge income booking"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": true,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "So it was a decent pickup QoQ in the US cards NIM. I was wondering whether that's sort of a new baseline. It's been a bit choppy, that NIM print, as you've had the repricing actions from last year, the changing funding structure. Is this kind of a new benchmark level, we progress from here or is it going to continue to be quite choppy both up and down? And then also there's a bit of complexity in terms of how you book the hedge income within US cards. Just maybe a bit of a better understanding of the nuances there, whether it's through net interest income or other income and [inaudible].",
  "answer_quote": "So, we did see progression in the NIM and I expect to see further progression from here. And that's really coming from the repricing actions which continue to mature, as you say, we took them last year, but, customers need to spend on the new terms and conditions for those to become live, and we continue to grow a deposit. We're around 73% [core deposits] now and we expect that to get to over 75%. That's our objective and you can see that on the slide and there is a differential in margin between those broker deposits and direct to retail deposits. Slide 25, if you want to have a look at that. So, the other thing that's going to help us progress Jordan, is, bringing on GM. So, GM is a higher margin because it's a retail book, but the risk adjusted margin is very good. So, you can see that, remembering Q3, we're going to onboard the back book of GM. We're already originating on the front book, so you're going to see further progress from here I think, in terms of that NIM. And just in terms of the two, quirky things that we've talked about before. We're now starting to book those on a forward basis in a different way. So, you're going to see the hedging come flowing into NII. So previously, the way we hedged this, you saw the margin compression from any rate reduction coming through in the NIM and you saw the offsetting income in non- NII. You're now going to see those geographically in the same place, bringing it into alignment with the group. And the third thing is, whilst it's not a massive matter in the quarter, previously what we've done is where we've had large pools of cash on the balance sheet used to pay down securitisation, they were included in that NIM calculation on an ongoing basis. Again, in alignment with the group, we will exclude those. So, I think some of that will take some of the choppiness that you've seen quarter to quarter out of the NIM also, Jordan. But the, most important thing is this forward momentum that's going to come from pricing and mix really. Okay, thank you.",
  "reason": "The response directly addresses the question about the new baseline for US card NIM, its future stability, and the complexities of hedge income booking, providing a clear stance and high evidence level with numeric evidence and forward guidance."
}
